ada: deployed variant small-seq-kernel v2 + paged-kv/evict-tweak at 09:02 UTC. noticing p99 jump on continuous-batcher. anyone seeing the same? :eyes:

piotr: saw a blip. can you paste the perf numbers?

ada: copying from metrics dashboard:
```
batcher.tokens_per_sec: baseline 8200 -> 8100 (-1.2%)
batcher.latency.p50: 28ms -> 30ms
batcher.latency.p95: 78ms -> 96ms
batcher.latency.p99: 180ms -> 340ms  <-- big jump
kernel.cpu.util: +6% on small-seq nodes
paged_kv.evictions/s: 680 -> 4200
```
Link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/xyz/continuous-batcher?from=now-1h

sam: whoa paged_kv evictions x6. looks like KV thrash when small sequences hit paged path. may be causing longer scheduler waits + kernel fallback.

jen: did the rollout change admission tokens or token_budget targets?

ada: rollout only changed kernel selection rule: prefer small-seq kernel when mean_seq_len < 24 AND kv_residency < 0.7. we also lowered the paged-kv prefetch window for memory headroom. no token_budget change.

piotr: interesting. evictions spike suggests we evicted hot prefixes mid-request, causing page faults and KV fetch stalls. continuous batcher then holds batches waiting for kernel. that explains p99. can you share a flamegraph or prof?

ada: attaching quick perf dump (excerpt):
```
# top stacks (samples)
1) runtime::paged_kv::page_fault_handler +30% samples
2) batcher::wait_for_kv +22%
3) kernel::small_seq_attention::flush_wait +18%
4) network::client_read +6%
```

infra-bot: deploy/1974005118: rollout small-seq-kernel v2 -> 40% ok

sam: two hypotheses: (A) small-seq kernel increases inline KV lookups due to different caching pattern, raising eviction churn; (B) lowered prefetch window means more synchronous page fetches. both amplify queueing under continuous batching.

piotr: quick mitigation ideas:
- bump token_budget target per-batch by +15% for small-seq nodes (more tokens -> smaller batches -> fewer concurrent KV streams)
- add KV-residency gate to batch admission: if kv_eviction_rate > threshold, degrade kernel selection to fallback (flash attention + larger seq batching)
- introduce soft backoff: limit concurrent batches that require paged-kv reads per GPU

ada: prototyped admission gate in ~30 lines, works locally. pseudocode:
```
if (kv.eviction_rate > 1k/s) {
  prefer_kernel = FLASH_DEFAULT
  token_budget *= 0.85
} else if (mean_seq_len < 24 && kv.residency > 0.75) {
  prefer_kernel = SMALL_SEQ
}
```

jen: can we A/B test this? put gate on canary subset (10%) and compare p99, throughput, and paged_kv.evictions. also measure token_efficiency (tokens consumed / useful_tokens).

sam: agree. also add a new prometheus metric: batcher.kv_wait_ms per-request so we can T-break where waits dominate.

piotr: quick safety: if p99 > 300ms revert rollout. set automation to roll back after 10m sustained.

ada: created canary rollout 1974005299 with admission-gate enabled on 10% small-seq nodes. monitoring -> grafana panel pinned.

infra-bot: canary/1974005299: started at 09:21 UTC -> 10% traffic

piotr: nice. also add a lightweight tracer tag on requests that got admitted vs gated so we can correlate quality/regressions.

jen: i'll own the dashboard comparisons. sam can you add the kv_wait_ms metric?

sam: on it, sending PR in a bit.

ada: note for follow-up: possible longer-term fix is to adjust paged-kv prefetch heuristics to be sequence-length aware and kernel-aware. small_seq kernel expects hot KV prefixes; we should bias prefetch accordingly.

piotr: agree. for now gate + canary + rollback threshold. will reconvene after 30m of canary data. :shipit:

ada: thanks all. ping me if you see anomalies.

jen: FYI pinned logs: ``[batch_id=0x7f3a] wait_for_kv: page fault 0.12s -> fetched 1.1MB``

sam: PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4823 -> adds kv_wait_ms and admission gate flag

ada: decision: keep rollout paused on remaining hosts until canary confirms.

piotr: ack.
